questions.q: From the given information, select the suitable law of chemical combination: Cupric Carbonate — Natural sample: 51.35% Cu, 9.74% C, 38.91% O; Synthetic sample: 51.35% Cu, 9.74% C, 38.91% O.
options: Gay Lussac's Law of Gaseous Volumes
questions.explanation: Since natural and synthetic samples of the same compound have identical elemental composition by mass, this illustrates the Law of Definite (Constant) Proportions.

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II and select the correct option (Based on mole concept):
List - I: (a) 2 moles of ethene (b) Molar mass is equal to 66 g (c) 1 g of H$_2$ (d) 2 moles of water vapours
List - II: (i) 11.2 L volume at STP (ii) 56 g (iii) 12.04 $\times$ 10$^{23}$ molecules (iv) 1.5 mole of CO$_2$
options: a - ii, b - iv, c - i, d - iii
a - iii, b - i, c - iv, d - ii
a - i, b - iv, c - ii, d - iii
a - ii, b - iii, c - i, d - iv
questions.explanation: 2 mol ethene weighs 56 g (a-ii); a molar mass of 66 g equals the mass of 1.5 mol CO$_2$ (44 g/mol) (b-iv); 1 g H$_2$ = 0.5 mol occupies 11.2 L at STP (c-i); 2 mol water vapour contains 12.04$\times$10$^{23}$ molecules (d-iii).

questions.q: Select the INCORRECT statement/s from the following: (a) 22 books have infinite significant figures. (b) In the answer of calculation 2.5 × 1.25, has four significant figures. (c) Zero's preceding to first non-zero digit are significant. (d) In the answer of calculation 12.11 + 18.0 + 1.012 has three significant figures
questions.explanation: 2.5×1.25=3.125 should be rounded to 2 significant figures (least precise factor), not four, so (b) is wrong; leading zeros before the first non-zero digit are never significant, so (c) is also wrong; 12.11+18.0+1.012=31.122 rounds to 31.1 (3 sig figs), so (d) is correct. Hence only (b) and (c) are incorrect.

questions.q: 0.48 g of an organic compound on complete combustion produced 0.22 g of CO$_2$. The percentage of C in the given organic compound is:
questions.explanation: %C = (12/44) $\times$ (mass of CO$_2$/mass of compound) $\times$ 100 = (12/44) $\times$ (0.22/0.48) $\times$ 100 = 12.5%.

questions.q: For which one of the following mixtures is composition uniform throughout?
questions.explanation: A dilute aqueous sugar solution is a homogeneous mixture, so its composition is uniform throughout.

questions.q: Temperature of 25 $^\circ$C in Fahrenheit and Kelvin scale respectively are
The volume of 2.8 g of CO at 27 °C and 0.821 atm. pressure is (R = 0.08210 lit. atm. K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)
A pure compound contains 2.4 g of C, 1.2 × 10$^{23}$ atoms of H, 0.2 moles of oxygen atoms. Its empirical formula is
When the absolute temperature of ideal gas is doubled and pressure is halved, the volume of gas
options: will be half of original volume
will be 4 times the original volume
will be 2 times the original volume
will be 1/4th times the original volume
questions.explanation: From PV = nRT, V$_2$ = nR(2T)/(P/2) = 4 × (nRT/P) = 4V$_1$.

questions.q: 0.4 g of dihydrogen is made to react with 7.1 g of dichlorine to form hydrogen chloride. The volume of hydrogen chloride formed at 273 K and 1 bar pressure is
questions.explanation: Moles: H$_2$ = 0.2, Cl$_2$ = 7.1/71 = 0.1 (limiting). H$_2$+Cl$_2\to$2HCl gives 0.2 mol HCl; at 273K, 1 bar molar volume is 22.7 L, so V = 0.2$\times$22.7 = 4.54 L.

questions.q: A gas mixture contains 25% He and 75% CH$_4$ by volume at a given temperature and pressure. The percentage by mass of methane in the mixture is approximately
questions.explanation: For 100 mol mixture: 25 mol He = 100 g, 75 mol CH$_4$ = 1200 g; mass % CH$_4$ = 1200/1300 $\approx$ 92%.

questions.q: The mass of AgCl precipitated when a solution containing 11.70 g of NaCl is added to a solution containing 3.4 g of AgNO$_3$ is [Atomic mass of Ag = 108, Atomic mass of Na = 23]
questions.explanation: Moles NaCl = 11.70/58.5 = 0.2; moles AgNO3 = 3.4/170 = 0.02 (limiting reagent); moles AgCl formed = 0.02, mass = 0.02 $\times$ 143.5 = 2.87 g.

questions.q: 1.0 g of Mg is burnt with 0.28 g of O$_2$ in a closed vessel. Which reactant is left in excess and how much ?
questions.explanation: Moles Mg = 1.0/24 = 0.0417 mol; moles O$_2$ = 0.28/32 = 0.00875 mol. Reaction 2Mg + O$_2$ $\to$ 2MgO needs 0.0175 mol Mg for the O$_2$ available, so Mg is in excess by (0.0417-0.0175)$\times$24 = 0.58 g.

questions.q: If $3.01 \times 10^{20}$ molecules are removed from 98 mg of H$_2$SO$_4$, then number of moles of H$_2$SO$_4$ left are
questions.explanation: Moles of H$_2$SO$_4$ initially = 98 mg / 98 g mol$^{-1}$ = $1\times10^{-3}$ mol = $6.022\times10^{20}$ molecules; removing $3.01\times10^{20}$ molecules leaves $3.012\times10^{20}$ molecules = $0.5\times10^{-3}$ mol.

questions.q: The number of oxygen atoms in 4.4 gm of CO$_2$ is,
questions.explanation: Moles of CO$_2$ = 4.4/44 = 0.1 mol, giving 0.2 mol O atoms = $1.2 \times 10^{23}$ atoms.

questions.q: An organic compound contains C = 40%, H = 13.33% and N = 46.67%. Its emperical formula is
questions.explanation: Moles: C=40/12=3.33, H=13.33/1=13.33, N=46.67/14=3.33; ratio C:H:N = 1:4:1, giving the empirical formula CH$_4$N.

questions.q: 0.30 g of an organic compound containing C, H and Oxygen on combustion yields 0.44 g CO$_2$ and 0.18 g H$_2$O. If one mol of compound weighs 60, then molecular formula of the compound is
questions.explanation: Mass of C = 0.44$\times$12/44 = 0.12 g, mass of H = 0.18$\times$2/18 = 0.02 g, mass of O = 0.30-0.12-0.02 = 0.16 g; mole ratio C:H:O = 0.01:0.02:0.01 = 1:2:1 gives empirical formula CH$_2$O (mass 30); since molar mass is 60, molecular formula is C$_2$H$_4$O$_2$.

questions.q: What amount of dioxygen (in gram) contains 1.8 $\times$ 10$^{22}$ molecules?
questions.explanation: Moles of O$_2$ = 1.8$\times$10$^{22}$/6.022$\times$10$^{23}$ $\approx$ 0.03 mol; mass = 0.03 $\times$ 32 g/mol $\approx$ 0.960 g.

questions.q:
10 g of a mixture of BaO and CaO requires 100 cm$^3$ of 2.5 M HCl to react completely. The percentage of calcium oxide in the mixture is approximately

(Given: molar mass of BaO = 153)
questions.explanation: Let x g BaO and (10-x) g CaO; moles HCl = 0.1×2.5 = 0.25 mol; equivalents: 2(x/153) + 2((10-x)/56) = 0.25; solving gives x ≈ 4.74 g BaO, so CaO ≈ 5.26 g, i.e. ≈ 52.6% CaO.

questions.q: 25 cm$^3$ of oxalic acid completely neutralised 0.064 g of sodium hydroxide. Molarity of the oxalic acid solution is
questions.explanation: Moles NaOH = 0.064/40 = 0.0016 mol; oxalic acid (diprotic) needs 2 mol NaOH per mol acid, so moles acid = 0.0008 mol; molarity = 0.0008/0.025 = 0.032 M.

questions.q: The number of water molecules present in a drop of water weighing 0.018 gm is
Empirical formula of a compound is CH$_2$O and its molecular mass is 90, the molecular formula of the compound is
questions.explanation: Empirical formula mass of CH$_2$O = 30; n = 90/30 = 3, so molecular formula = (CH$_2$O)$_3$ = C$_3$H$_6$O$_3$.

questions.q: The mass of 112 cm$^3$ of NH$_3$ gas at STP is
The total number of electrons in 18 ml of water (density = 1 g ml$^{-1}$) is
questions.explanation: 18 ml water = 18 g = 1 mole = 6.02×10$^{23}$ molecules; each H$_2$O has 10 electrons, so total = 10×6.02×10$^{23}$=6.02×10$^{24}$.

questions.q: The equivalent mass of a certain bivalent metal is 20. The molecular mass of its anhydrous chloride is
questions.explanation: Atomic mass of metal = equivalent mass × valency = 20×2=40. Chloride MCl$_2$: molecular mass $=40+2\times35.5=111$.

questions.q: A mixture of $CaCl_2$ and $NaCl$ weighing 4.44 g is treated with sodium carbonate solution to precipitate all the calcium ions as calcium carbonate. The calcium carbonate so obtained is heated strongly to get 0.56 g of $CaO$. The percentage of $NaCl$ in the mixture is .................. [Atomic mass of $Ca=40$].
questions.explanation: Moles $CaO$ = 0.56/56 = 0.01 mol = moles $Ca$; mass $CaCl_2$ = 0.01 × 111 = 1.11 g, so $NaCl$ = 4.44 − 1.11 = 3.33 g, which is 75% of the mixture.

questions.q: 50 cm$^3$ of 0.2 N $HCl$ is titrated against 0.1 N $NaOH$ solution. The titration was discontinued after adding 50 cm$^3$ of $NaOH$. The remaining titration is completed by adding 0.5 N $KOH$. The volume of $KOH$ required for completing the titration is ...........
questions.explanation: Milliequivalents of $HCl$ = 50×0.2 = 10; milliequivalents of $NaOH$ added = 50×0.1 = 5; the remaining 5 meq are neutralized by 0.5 N $KOH$, needing 5/0.5 = 10 cm$^3$.

questions.q: A mixture of $CaCl_2$ and $NaCl$ weighing 4.44 g is treated with sodium carbonate solution to precipitate all the $Ca^{+2}$ ions as calcium carbonate. The calcium carbonate so obtained is heated strongly to get 0.56 g of $CaO$. The percentage of $NaCl$ in the mixture (atomic mass of $Ca$ = 40) is ...............
questions.explanation: Moles CaO = 0.56/56 = 0.01 = moles Ca, mass Ca = 0.4 g, mass CaCl$_2$ = 0.01 $\times$ 111 = 1.11 g, so NaCl = 4.44 - 1.11 = 3.33 g, i.e. 75%.

questions.q: 50 cm$^3$ of 0.2 N $HCl$ is titrated against 0.1 N $NaOH$ solution. The titration is discontinued after adding 50 cm$^3$ of $NaOH$. The remaining titration is completed by adding 0.5 N $KOH$. The volume of $KOH$ required for completing the titration is ...............
questions.explanation: Milli-equivalents of HCl = 10; NaOH added = 5; remaining HCl = 5 meq, needing 5/0.5 = 10 cm$^3$ of 0.5 N KOH.

questions.q: In which one of the following, does the given amount of chlorine exert the least pressure in a vessel of capacity 1 dm$^3$ at 273K?
questions.explanation: 0.0355 g Cl$_2$ = 0.0005 mol, the smallest number of moles among the options, so it exerts the least pressure (pressure is proportional to moles at fixed V, T).

questions.q: Excess of carbon dioxide is passed through 50 ml of 0.5 M calcium hydroxide solution. After the completion of the reaction, the solution was evaporated to dryness. The solid calcium carbonate was completely neutralised with 0.1 N Hydrochloric acid. The volume of Hydrochloric acid required is (At. mass of calcium = 40)
questions.explanation: Moles Ca(OH)$_2$ = 0.025; evaporation converts any bicarbonate back to 0.025 mol CaCO$_3$. CaCO$_3$ + 2HCl needs 0.05 mol HCl, so volume = 0.05/0.1 = 500 cm$^3$.

questions.q: A bivalent metal has an equivalent mass of 32. The molecular mass of the metal nitrate is
questions.explanation: Atomic mass = equivalent mass $\times$ valency = 64. M(NO$_3$)$_2$ mass = 64 + 2(62) = 188.
